title: A study on tolerable waiting time: how long are Web users willing to wait?
authors_venue_year: Nah, F. F.-H. (2004). *Behaviour & Information Technology*, 23(3),
notes: Real, accessible study (Nah, 2004, 70 subjects). Directly measures that a loading indicator/feedback bar significantly extends users' patience before abandoning a blank/unresponsive page (13s to 38s average wait) - this supports E-019's 'implement a meaningful loading state' fix specifically. Caveat: dated (2004, dial-up era), small sample, studies broken-link waits rather than JS-render delays specifically, but the underlying mechanism (blank page + no feedback = abandonment; feedback = more patience) transfers well.
